core_obligations: Record that the etale case follows directly from the construction of the reduction (proof lines 2930-2932).
In the smooth case, observe that the base change of the reduction of the target along the morphism is smooth over a reduced algebraic space, hence reduced (proof lines 2932-2936).

difficulty_reason: For a morphism of formal algebraic spaces which is representable by algebraic spaces and smooth, the lemma asserts that the reduction of the source is the base change of the reduction of the target (statement lines 2922-2928). The proof notes that in the etale case this follows directly from the construction of the reduction, and then treats the smooth case: the base change of the reduction of the target along the morphism is a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces, hence a reduced algebraic space by the corresponding locality statement, and the universal property of the reduction then shows that the canonical morphism from the reduction of the source to it is an isomorphism (proof lines 2930-2940). The claim is H2: after the etale case is delegated to the construction, the smooth case is a genuine two-step argument, using reducedness under smooth morphisms and the universal property of the reduction.
